name: otr-many-facts
about: An over-the-road job with many facts: enough for five angles that differ in kind. Its brief is shaped as a real opening's (`openingSubjectMatter`): the job details are the equipment and the schedule, and every benefit is a listed term.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: Family owned, and the owner still drives

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook equipment_first (equipment first) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $402.10 in the last 28 days over 30100 impressions and brought 14 leads, $28.72 per lead.

output.audience: Experienced Class A drivers who already run over the road, on reefer or similar freight, and are used to a wide running area. They have a mileage job now. A plainly stated pay per mile, a newer truck and no-touch freight would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, shown over a reefer rig rolling on the highway.
angles.proof: The opening states the pay per mile for over-the-road reefer runs.
angles.why: Pay is the plainest fact this job has, and no earlier ad of ours led with it. Nothing has been measured for this hook or for formats, so this is a test.

angles.idea: Lead with the late-model truck the driver would be handed, parked and clean.
angles.why: This pairing brought leads under the benchmark pause level, though the lead count is thin and not proof. Keep it as the reference; nothing is measured on formats.

angles.idea: Say plainly what the job asks: over the road across the stated running area, with the experience and weeks figures as written.
angles.proof: The job states the running area, a years figure and a weeks figure, and that the runs are over the road.
angles.why: A plain statement lets drivers who want local work pass by before they become a lead. Untested here; the office should confirm what the weeks and years figures refer to.

angles.idea: Lead with the week as lived in the cab: the pet policy and no-touch freight, seen from the driver's seat.
angles.proof: The opening offers a pet policy and no-touch freight.
angles.why: Over-the-road drivers live in the truck, so these facts speak to the week itself. Nothing has been measured for this hook or for formats.

angles.idea: Lead with who the carrier is, family owned with an owner who still drives, and list the benefits on a plain ground.
angles.proof: The job's own words say family owned and the owner still drives; it offers health insurance, a retirement plan and paid time off.
angles.why: Words carry this ad, so a plain ground suits it. No earlier ad used this hook, so nothing has been measured.
